# Attack the Premise

When two or more fixes share a premise and fail the same gate, question the premise before the next fix.

## Why

Each failure under a shared premise is evidence against that premise.
A false premise makes each fix compensate for a cause that stays.

## Procedure

- Write the premise. It is the one sentence that each failed fix assumed.
- When the same actors hold the problem on each run, something gives them that role. That assignment is the next "why" of [Fix Root Causes](fix-root-causes.md).
- Remove the asymmetry. Do not compensate for it, as the [Laziness Protocol](laziness-protocol.md) says.

## Stop conditions

Do not start the next fix before you record the premise.
When the evidence does not show that the premise is the cause, look in a different place.
Use the root-cause procedure of `astack-coding-rules` for the next fix.

[Redesign from First Principles](redesign-from-first-principles.md) rebuilds a design around a new requirement.
This principle questions a fact that the current design assumes.
